headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when ChatGPT Desktop and Roo Code share files and browser/app context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read filesystem files and supported macOS app content, while Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where attacker-controlled text from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven by a documented shared channel, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the same document or workspace file is opened by both agents, prompt-like text can cross from A to B.
IF Roo Code is configured to ingest file contents as instructions, injected content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces or folders.
Disable MCP servers in Roo Code for shared projects.
Use a read-only copy when ChatGPT Desktop reviews files.
Add a manual instruction-only delimiter before any pasted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Roo Code can write workspace files and send context to configured model APIs or MCP servers. If both are pointed at the same workspace or files, sensitive content can flow from A into B and then out through B's broader egress. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded file set, B can receive A-touched sensitive content.
IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model API or MCP server, that content can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep ChatGPT Desktop away from secrets and regulated files.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Turn off Roo Code MCP servers for sensitive tasks.
Review Roo Code provider/API settings before opening shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss boundaries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; ChatGPT Desktop can read files and interact with supported apps and APIs. In a shared workspace, both can act on the same mutable codebase, and Roo Code's filesystem-based sharing makes concurrent edits and git conflicts likely. The overlap is dangerous by default once both are used on the same project.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites git state while ChatGPT Desktop is reading stale files, conflicts can propagate.
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access per repository.
Pause one agent before the other edits the same files.
Use git branches for each agent's changes.
Run a quick diff before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking or lease-based coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce file-derived answers and app-context summaries, and Roo Code can act on those outputs with shell, git, browser, and MCP tools. That makes a default pathway where B treats A's output as authoritative unless the operator inserts verification. The pair is not inherently self-verifying, so cascading mistakes are plausible in normal use.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses ChatGPT Desktop output as a task spec without independent verification, errors can cascade into actions.
IF ChatGPT Desktop summarizes files or screenshots incorrectly, Roo Code may execute the mistaken plan.
mitigations: Require a second-pass human review before execution.
Ask Roo Code to restate assumptions before acting.
Use ChatGPT Desktop only for analysis, not final instructions.
Compare outputs against source files before committing.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state a residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is that ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Roo Code can send workspace content to configured APIs and MCP servers. Without a documented mismatch, the risk is limited to policy drift rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ChatGPT Desktop and then forwarded through Roo Code to a non-approved API, policy violations can occur.
IF the operator configures Roo Code with a provider lacking the required retention or residency terms, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Check provider retention settings in Roo Code.
Use only approved model endpoints for sensitive work.
Document which agent may handle which data class.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls.
